title: AssetDescriptor
description: One asset, described as a plain object: its type, an optional source, and the type's options as further properties. - A string `source` is a locator. It goes through variant selection, the base path, the cache and the network, and two descriptors with the same type, locator and identity-relevant options share one resource. - Any other `source` value is handed to the type's factory as it is: nothing is fetched or cached. Descriptors sharing the same source object (or the same primitive value) share one resource. - Without a `source`, the factory builds from the options alone. Such a descriptor is identified by its type's `resourceIdentity` when the type defines one, and otherwise by the descriptor object itself: release it with the same object, or release the loaded resource. Only a locator can be held by a catalog, handed out by `get()`, loaded at background priority or saved as a portable reference. A plain object with an own `type` property is always read as a descriptor, never as a named load group.
